name: Captain Odell
examine: Odell keeps his desk clear. The only paper visible is a draft headed GAS-MAIN — penciled, then abandoned. His eyes never leave your collar.

lines: Six members are dead. The other two are a filing matter. You understand the difference.
I am not asking you to invent a gas main. I am asking you not to invent a scandal.
Write what will hold. Not what will haunt.

name: Father Behan
examine: Behan's hands smell of incense and soap. The parish register is open to a page he is not reading.

lines: They asked me twice to sit with them. I declined twice. A priest knows when a table is set for something other than supper.
Dr. Fenn insisted — twice — on being buried beside the club rather than beside his wife. I wrote it down. I did not ask why.
Toward the end they stopped speaking of power. They spoke, tenderly, of her.

name: Mrs. Kessler
examine: The shop is closed. She stands behind the counter as if the day might still open. A ledger lies face-down.

lines: He wore his good coat to a club that used him and despised him in the same evening.
Shop money bought him a chair among men who called him tradesman to his face.
He carried a parcel wrapped in butcher paper into a private room once. He left without it. He never said what was in it.

name: Club Barman
examine: He polishes a glass that is already clean. He does not look at your badge. He does not look away from it either.

lines: Last Thursday of every month. Over two years. Six chairs. The sixth never signed a bill, never came by the front door.
Kessler said it more than once: She'll have us home. She's no different from any mother.
I refill glasses. I do not invent meanings for what I overhear.

name: Estate Crew
examine: Three men at the tunnel mouth beyond the birches. Flat coats. Flat faces. They do not fidget. They do not volunteer.

lines: We do not go down there.
The ground is wrong. That is enough.
Curiosity is not a duty of this employment.
